content: Post-viral cough is a persistent cough that occurs after a viral respiratory tract infection, such as the common cold or influenza, and it typically lasts for more than eight weeks. This condition is clinically recognized in European medical literature, although it is not commonly addressed in studies originating from the United States. Patients often experience recurrent episodes of post-viral cough. The heightened sensitivity of the respiratory tract in these cases can be demonstrated through inhalation cough challenge tests. One potential cause of post-viral cough is the continued activation of cough receptors in the respiratory tract, which remain upregulated even after the viral infection has resolved. Post-viral cough can be challenging to treat and may not respond well to standard therapies. Inhaled corticosteroids may provide relief for some patients. Generally, the management of post-viral cough follows similar approaches to the treatment of viral cough.
